title: When the Kiln Goes Out
logline: A potter's crew feeds a wood-fired kiln through an entire night, watching the wind and the colour of the flame, and only when the fuel stops and the fire finally dies down can the kiln cool enough to open.

object.note: Object 9 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject. Object 8, from Endings, may also recur as a fire is finally let go out.

thread_in.thread: Conditions that shape a season lead to a fire that lasts only as long as it is fed: a crew tending a wood-fired kiln through the night until it is let go out.

thread_out.thread: What arises by conditions can end by conditions: the kiln stops being fed, and the next film opens on something set down, a family's final payment on gold pawned years ago.

requirements: A traditional pottery workshop still firing by wood in a single overnight session
Access through a full night of work
A crew willing to show real losses, not only successful pots

suggestions.name: A traditional pottery-making village
suggestions.region: Kegalle or Kurunegala district (villages such as Molagoda are known for pottery)
suggestions.why: Low-country pottery villages in this area have long-standing traditions of wood-fired kilns.
suggestions.verify: Whether a specific workshop still fires by wood, rather than gas or electricity, and is willing to be filmed overnight must be confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: A fire lasts only as long as it is fed, and when the feeding stops it dies down. The texts say a living body, too, keeps going only while food and weather keep supporting it.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ගින්නක් පවතින්නේ දර දමන තාක් පමණක් වන්නාක් මෙන්, ජීවත් වන කයක් ද පවතින්නේ ආහාරය හා සෘතුව එයට පිහිට වන තාක් පමණක් බව අභිධර්මය උගන්වයි.
lesson.the_teaching: Margaya explains conditions with a match: the tip of the match and the side of the box both help make the flame, each in a different way, and if they helped in the same way one alone would be enough. The Paṭṭhāna names a presence condition, support simply by still being there, and the Pradeepika says the kamma-born body continues only with the support of weather and food, and without it a being dies. In the mind, the texts add, one moment supports the next by ceasing and making room for it.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Through the night the crew stacks wood, watches the wind and reads the colour of the flame, knowing the fire holds only while fuel keeps arriving. Near dawn the feeding stops and the fire is allowed to die down, and only then can the kiln cool and be opened; the viewer sees that the ending belongs to the process, as pots are lifted out, some cracked, most whole.

key_terms.en: presence: support by still being there
absence: support by ceasing and making room
nutriment condition: what sustains body and mind

lesson.caution: It is not a slogan that 'letting go makes room for the new': in the texts, support by ceasing describes one moment of mind giving way to the next, and the kiln is only an everyday echo of it.
lesson.builds_on: The monsoon film showed outer conditions strongly supporting inner states; the kiln shows the other side of support, that what is held up by being fed ends when the feeding stops.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
